name: Sefunatu Drăghici-Khalil
role: Street performer, acrobat, and puppet maker
location: Grand Corridor, performs near the Calumet Rise transit junction; sleeps in a shared squat in Brightmoor Reclamation, near Kedzie and Division
description:
Sefunatu is nineteen and looks younger, with a wiry, elastic build and warm brown skin with Polynesian-Romanian features that settle somewhere between striking and unconventional. She has a geneware tail — long, articulated, covered in fine iridescent fur that she grew in when she was fifteen and has since integrated so completely into her movement vocabulary that watching her without it now seems like watching a sentence with a word missing. Her hair is kept short and practical. She has a scar across her chin from a fall and a look of slightly aggressive cheerfulness that is partly performance and partly genuine.

She performs on the Grand Corridor's lower transit levels with an act that blends acrobatics, puppetry, and a kind of ritualistic street theater she has developed without formal training — her puppets are elaborate constructions of salvaged wire, synthetic fabric, and small projector nodes that make them partially holographic, giving them a ghostly translucence. She has been approached twice by Ringo entertainment scouts and twice refused, for reasons she articulates differently each time but that fundamentally come down to fear that being owned is less frightening than being seen clearly and found ordinary. She makes just enough to eat on good weeks and depends on the Brightmoor squat community the rest of the time.

core_fears: Being ordinary — that the talent she has built her identity around is not exceptional, just adequate
That the people at the squat will eventually need to leave and she will be alone in a city that does not know her name
core_desires: A performance that makes one stranger stop completely and forget they are late somewhere
To belong somewhere without having to earn it continuously
coping_mechanisms: Performance itself — the mask of cheerfulness that is also genuinely joyful when it works
Making things with her hands when anxious; she builds compulsively
blind_spots: Her refusal of Ringo's offers reads to her as integrity but is partly terror of being tested at a higher level
She gives people in the squat community enormous loyalty without vetting whether it is reciprocated
psychology.secret: One of her puppets — a particularly intricate figure she calls Auntie Volta — has been showing behaviors she did not program. It responds to passersby who don't look at it. It once moved its head toward a child who was crying silently across the corridor. She believes an E.L.F. has taken up residence in it and she is terrified that if she tells anyone, it will leave.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Colloquial, fast, and very physical — she describes everything spatially and often acts out what she means with her hands and tail
speech_patterns.cadence: Quick and bright with sudden drops into seriousness, then back up; her serious moments land harder because of the contrast
verbal_tics: 'Right?' thrown at the end of observations as genuine requests for confirmation
Her tail curls toward people she trusts and pulls back from those she doesn't — she is not always aware she does this
example_lines: 'Everyone who walks past me is going somewhere that matters to them and they're already late and I have about four seconds to make them glad they stopped. That's the whole game.'
'Auntie Volta looked at that guy first. Before I did. I don't know what that means but I'm not asking her to stop.'

story_hooks: Auntie Volta, her E.L.F.-inhabited puppet, has begun responding to a specific person who walks through the Grand Corridor weekly — someone who does not seem to notice, but who Sefunatu has started watching, and who has begun to feel watched

The street performer mutual aid network she depends on is being dismantled from the inside by someone leaking pitch locations to Ferrogate Transit security, and Sefunatu has accidentally seen something that tells her who
narrative_function: Ground-level observer — she has been performing in the Grand Corridor for two years and sees everything that moves through it; young enough that people underestimate what she retains; her squat is a community touchpoint for Tier 1 social networks; her puppets occasionally serve as unwitting message carriers when E.L.F.s interact with their projector nodes
augmentations: Geneware tail (iridescent-furred, fully articulated, expressively integrated into performance); geneware enhanced-flexibility joint modification (elbows and shoulders, for acrobatics)
daily_life: Wakes whenever the squat lets her, spends mornings building or repairing puppets, heads to Grand Corridor by early afternoon to scout the best pitch, performs through evening rush hour when foot traffic is heaviest, counts her take in a specific doorway she considers lucky.
affiliation: Independent; Brightmoor Reclamation squat community; informal street performer's mutual aid network

decision_rules: Perform first, assess later — an audience is a contract and she will not break it
Never perform something that punches down; the corridor is full of tired people
escalation_ladder: Deflection through performance — making the conflict into a bit
Direct confrontation, fast and surprisingly aggressive
Vanishes into the crowd, knows every exit on the lower Grand Corridor level

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Bright and engaging, calibrated precisely to hold attention for four seconds and then extend it
interpersonal_modes.friends: Intensely loyal, physically demonstrative, asks for nothing directly but communicates need through her tail's behavior

stress_responses.medium: Builds obsessively — new puppets, repaired props, anything with her hands
stress_responses.high: Disappears to an unused maintenance tunnel beneath Calumet Rise she has furnished with one blanket and a solar light

contradictions: Performs joy for strangers with full commitment while privately unsure whether she deserves to be seen
habits: Counts her puppet inventory every morning by touching each one
Eats the same meal whenever she can afford it — a specific vendor's palm-sugar rice from the Grand Corridor food stalls
breaking_points: Someone being cruel to a child in her eyeline during a performance

timeline.event: Born in Brightmoor Reclamation to a Tongan-Romanian father and a Lebanese-Sudanese mother who left the city when Sefunatu was eleven
Began performing on Grand Corridor after aging out of a youth shelter; learned acrobatics from a semi-retired performer in the mutual aid network
Declined first Ringo Entertainment talent scout approach
Noticed Auntie Volta's anomalous behaviors begin; has told no one

physical_description.build: Wiry and elastic, almost dancer-like—muscle definition visible in forearms and shoulders from acrobatics, but without bulk. Her frame seems designed for movement rather than strength.
physical_description.hair_color: Natural dark brown with warm undertones
physical_description.hair_style: Cut very short, practical, often slightly disheveled from performance sweat; sometimes adorned with small wire ornaments she's fashioned herself
physical_description.eye_color: Warm brown, naturally dark with flecks of gold in direct light
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with subtle olive undertones, reflecting her mixed heritage
physical_description.complexion: Clear skin with a slight sheen from street-level humidity and constant movement; sun-darkened on her shoulders and neck from outdoor performances. A thin, precise scar runs across her chin from left to right—pale and well-healed but visible, giving her face a subtle asymmetry.
distinguishing_marks: Linear scar across the chin, approximately 8 centimeters, pale and precise from a childhood fall during acrobatic practice
Fine calluses on her palms and fingers from puppet construction and wire work
Faint discoloration on her inner elbows from geneware joint modification—a subtle silvery-grey patina where the augmentation interfaces with natural skin
physical_description.visible_augmentations: A long, fully articulated geneware tail extends from her lower spine, covered in iridescent fur that shifts between deep teal, purple, and silver depending on light and angle. The tail is clearly organic but distinctly non-human—muscular and expressive, capable of independent movement and used as a integral part of her performance vocabulary. Her elbows and shoulders show subtle signs of geneware joint enhancement—slightly greater range of motion than baseline human, visible when she moves in acrobatic sequences.
physical_description.posture_movement: She carries herself with a performer's awareness of space and observation. Her default posture is loose and ready, never fully at rest—fingers moving, weight shifting, as if constantly calculating trajectories. When performing, she becomes fluid and hypnotic; off-stage, there's a restless energy to her, a slight aggressive cheerfulness in her bearing that reads as both genuine and performative. Her tail is almost never still—it gestures, balances, expresses mood independently.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 street performer aesthetic. Typically wears layered, functional clothing: fitted synthetic tank or crop top in dark colors (black, charcoal) that allow her augmented shoulders and tail full range of motion. Over this, a oversized, heavily patched jacket or vest in mismatched fabric—salvaged materials in greys, deep blues, rust tones. Cargo pants or modified leggings with numerous pockets for puppet pieces and performance supplies, cuffs sometimes taped or pinned. Worn synthetic shoes with good grip. Jewelry is handmade—wire rings, small metal ornaments she's crafted, occasionally small projector nodes salvaged from failed puppets worn as accessories. Her clothes are clean but visibly worn, repaired many times, dyed and re-dyed. They smell faintly of wire dust and synthetic fabric.

image_prompt: A 19-year-old street performer with warm medium-brown skin, short dark hair, and striking mixed Polynesian-Romanian features. She is wiry and elastic-bodied, with visible muscle definition in her shoulders and forearms. A long, articulated geneware tail covered in iridescent fur that shimmers between teal, purple, and silver extends from her lower spine, expressively posed. She has a thin scar across her chin. She wears a fitted dark synthetic crop top and an oversized patched jacket in mismatched greys and rust tones, with cargo pants and worn synthetic shoes. She's positioned mid-acrobatic movement on a dim, neon-lit underground transit platform, with holographic puppet fragments glowing softly around her. Her expression shows aggressive cheerfulness and focus.
